title: The ordered endpoint pullback is an etale hypercover
statement: Let X be quasi-compact and quasi-separated, let U,V be etale hypercovers [def-weil-pbc-etale-hypercover], and let a,b:U to V. The explicit ordered endpoint pullback K [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-ordinal-path] is an etale hypercover. More precisely, a matching datum of K together with a compatible degree n simplex of U has local lifts to K_n.

source.place: Tags 01GN and 01GS, relative matching covers and the endpoint construction

proof.text: From a matching datum q:T to M_n(K) and a compatible simplex u:T to U_n, form the lower proper-face family in the ordered path object by the second projection of K. The matching compatibility and endpoint pullback equations identify its endpoints with u followed by a and b.

Glue the full endpoint simplices and this lower family on their finite nonempty union A_n in Delta[2n+1]. Ordinary finite-simplex lifting gives, over an etale covering of T, degree 2n+1 simplices of V restricting to this family.

Combine each extended V-simplex with u using the evaluated endpoint pullback. Its first and second projections and all proper-face generator equations identify the lower K-faces. The proper-face matching universal property therefore says that these are local lifts of q.

For absolute matching covers, pull U_n to M_n(U) back along the natural map M_n(K) to M_n(U). Its projection to M_n(K) is surjective by base change. Over this projection apply the preceding relative local lift. The small etale topology criterion says the covering points jointly surject onto that pullback; their lifts then surject onto M_n(K). This proves every canonical K matching arrow surjective, hence K is an etale hypercover.
